steps.title: What we'll do today
steps.html:
So far you've used Manual mode, where Claude asks every time it creates or edits a file. It's safe, but tiring when there's a lot to do.

Today you'll change the permission mode and learn when it's safe to change it.

  • Time: 15 minutes
  • You need: a computer that finished Desktop 4 (todo.txt in the Practice folder)

steps.title: Open the list of modes
steps.html:
1. Claude app → Code tab → + New to open a new chat. Folder: Practice.
  2. Click the Manual button under the typing box to open the list of modes.
ManualAsks every time before creating, editing or running commands. What you've used so far
Accept editsDoesn't ask for file edits and common file commands like making folders or moving files. Still asks for other commands
PlanDoesn't edit files; only makes a plan and shows it
AutoThe AI judges for itself whether actions match your request (we won't use it today)
steps.alt: Clicking the Manual button to open the list of modes

check.q: Can you see Manual, Accept edits and Plan in the list?

steps.title: If the list looks different
steps.html:
• Names vary a little by app version, e.g. Ask permissions (= Manual), Auto accept edits (= Accept edits), Plan mode (= Plan).
  • Auto may not appear depending on your account or model. That's fine.
  • If you see Bypass permissions, don't choose it. Step 7 explains why.

steps.title: Plan: have it make a plan first
steps.html:
1. Choose Plan from the list.
  2. Send the sentence below.

Claude only reads todo.txt and shows a plan for what it would do. The file stays as it is.
steps.alt: In Plan mode it shows a plan and doesn't change the file
steps.code: Make a plan to split todo.txt into urgent and later

check.q: Did it show only a plan, without changing the file?

steps.title: If it tries to edit instead of planning
steps.html:
• Check that the button under the typing box says Plan.
  • If Claude asks you something (e.g. what's urgent), answer it. That's part of planning.
  • If a permission card appears, click Deny, switch to Plan and send it again.

steps.title: If you like the plan, carry it out
steps.html:
1. Switch the mode back to Manual.
  2. Send the sentence below. When the permission card appears, read the red and green lines and click Allow.
If the app shows a button under the plan like Proceed with the plan, you can click that instead. It may change the mode, so check the button under the typing box.

Don't like the plan? While in Plan, ask for changes, e.g. "Leave out step 3 and plan again."
steps.code: Great, go ahead with that plan

check.q: Did you read and allow the card, and is todo.txt now split into two groups?

steps.title: If it didn't follow the plan
steps.html:
• In Plan it won't edit files. Switch the button to Manual and send it again.
  • Don't like the result? Say "Undo what you just did."

steps.title: Accept edits: edit without asking
steps.html:
1. Switch the mode to Accept edits.
  2. Send the sentence below.

This time it edits without a permission card. You can see what changed under Changes on the right.
steps.alt: In Accept edits mode it edits right away, and the change shows in Changes
steps.code: Add "Exercise" to the end of todo.txt

check.q: Was 'Exercise' added right away, without asking?

steps.title: If it still asks
steps.html:
• Check that the button under the typing box says Accept edits.
  • Commands other than file edits still ask in Accept edits. That's normal.

steps.title: Convenient, but you need to double-check
steps.html:
Accept edits is fast, but it doesn't show you changes first. Use it safely like this:

  • In a place where mistakes don't matter, like the Practice folder, for jobs that are clear and repetitive
  • When it's done, always skim the changes in Changes
  • If something went wrong: "Undo what you just did."

In folders with important documents, Manual is safer.

steps.title: Switch back to Manual
steps.html:
When you're done practising, switch the mode back to Manual. Until you're comfortable, Manual is your default.

A new chat may keep your last choice of mode. Make a habit of checking the button under the typing box whenever you start a new chat.

check.q: Does the button under the typing box say Manual now?

steps.title: If you can't find Manual
steps.html: Depending on the app version it may say Ask permissions. It's the same mode.

steps.title: Two modes to use with care
steps.html:
AutoThe AI judges for itself whether an action matches your request. Convenient, but it can judge wrong. Try it once you're comfortable, starting with unimportant jobs.
Bypass permissionsNever asks. Even the official docs say to use it only in isolated test environments. Don't use it. (It only shows up if you turn it on in Settings.)
Start with Manual, use Plan when you want a plan, and Accept edits for repetitive work in the Practice folder. Those three are all you need.

steps.title: 🎉 Desktop practice 5 done! What you learned
steps.html:
From installing to permission modes, you've learned all the basic controls.

ManualAsks every time. Your default
PlanPlan first, before a big job
Accept editsDoesn't ask for file edits. For repetitive work in the Practice folder. Check Changes afterwards
Auto · BypassOnce you're comfortable / don't use

Two things to remember

  1. Change the mode with the button under the typing box. Check it in every new chat.
  2. The less a mode asks, the more you need to check afterwards.

What you've learned so far

Install the app → create a file → read changes → new chat or continue → organize several files → permission modes. Now you can hand Claude simple jobs on your own. Next come undoing mistakes, showing it pictures, and real work like spreadsheets and documents.
